title: Lessee - Comparison of patient-related scattered radiation during bilateral radiology intervention using RadPads
summary: Due to the increasing need for minimally invasive therapies and the therefore more frequently performed angiographic interventions, there is an increased cumulative radiation exposure of the intervention personnel. This radiation exposure is mainly caused by scattered radiation emitted by the patient and can lead to health risks. The reduction in radiation exposure depends on the treatment performed. To date, there have been no prospective analyses of the benefits of RadPads. Bilateral interventions lend themselves to prospective side-by-side comparison. Therefore, the intervention should be performed on one side without and on the other side with the sterile patient pad.

interventions.name:
After routine inpatient admission for therapy of the prostate, education for the study takes place, which is not therapy-relevant.  There are no follow-up visits regarding the therapy, the study is completed with the intervention.
The study procedure is exemplified below using prostatic artery embo

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Indication for bilateral intervention
- Angiography suitable intervention with technical feasibility
- Routine preparation for prostate embolization
Exclusion criteria:
- No indication for bilateral intervention
- Technical problems with the use of the RadPad
